thread:
Jordan R: Hey team — quick Q on Accept-Model header fallback behavior for older SDKs. We're seeing clients without the header hitting /v1/generate and getting different models over time. What's the intended compatibility story here?

Leah P: Good catch. The intended rule historically was: if Accept-Model present -> honor it; if absent -> resolve alias 'default' -> map to the current default model. That mapping changed a couple of times and I think we never had a formal deprecation window documented.

Samir: Current runtime behavior (today): if Accept-Model is absent we resolve the account default alias. We've been planning to change the alias mapping from "v1-legacy" -> "v2-stable" next quarter. That WILL change what clients get when they don't set Accept-Model.

Kevin: So this is a breaking change for clients that assumed the server-chosen model would be stable. Suggestion: detect older SDKs (X-Redwood-SDK header) and keep old mapping for them for a fixed compatibility window.

Maya: Agree with Kevin. Also we should push the SDK to set an explicit Accept-Model when bumping to 2.x so users are explicit. Migration docs should show how to pin.

Jordan R: Proposal: rollout plan: 30-day canary (internal + opt-in customers), 60-day gradual rollout (percentage-based), final enforcement at 120 days after announcement. During canary/rollout, runtime exposes a config flag `compat.default_model_v1` that preserves legacy mapping for flagged accounts or SDK versions. Any objections?

Leah P: +1. Add a public docs notice and email at T-30 days. I want console visibility: show which alias maps to which model in account settings so customers can see impending changes.

Samir: Implementation notes: I can add a runtime feature flag and a UA-version check. Pseudocode below for clarity:
```http
GET /v1/generate
X-Redwood-SDK: redwood-js/1.4.0
Accept-Model: (absent)

-> Server resolution:
if Accept-Model missing:
  if X-Redwood-SDK < 2.0 && compat.default_model_v1 enabled for account:
     use "v1-legacy"
  else:
     use "v2-stable"
```
This keeps behavior stable for older SDKs while nudging newer clients to opt-in to the explicit header.

Kevin: Who owns comms and rollover? I can coordinate rollout percentage controls in the infra dashboard but need the flag toggles from Samir and a docs/email from Leah.

Jordan R: Ownership: Leah + Maya to draft deprecation announcement + migration guide; Samir to implement flag and telemetry; Kevin to wire rollout percentages and smoke tests; Jordan will own the rollout playbook and public timeline.

Leah P: Action items:
- Leah/Maya: draft announcement + console UI copy (due in 3 business days)
- Samir: runtime flag + UA check + metric emission (due EOW)
- Kevin: rollout gating + smoke tests (start after Samir PR lands)
- Jordan: public timeline + email recipients list

Maya: I'll add a migration note in the SDK repo showing how to set Accept-Model explicitly, with examples for JS and Python. Example: `Accept-Model: redwood/gpt-alt-2025` and fallback guidance.

Jordan R: Also request: emit a telemetry event `model_fallback_reason` with tags: `client_sdk_version`, `account_id`, `resolved_alias`, `resolved_model`. That will help us quantify impact during the rollout.

Samir: Good call. I'll add the event and a brief dashboard showing how many requests relied on compatibility fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for compat-flag branch -> staging @ 2105005488 :rocket:

Kevin: Can we get PR reviews this week? If Samir's PR lands by Thursday we can run a small staging canary Friday. :eyes:

Samir: I'm aiming to open the PR in the next 24h. Will tag reviewers: @Leah, @Kevin.

Jordan R: Thanks all — I'll circulate the timeline doc after this thread and link the migration snippets. If anyone thinks 120 days is too short/long speak up now.

Leah P: 120 days seems reasonable but let's make the opt-in canary obvious in the console so power users can pick it early. :+1:

Maya: I'll draft the SDK examples and send a PR to the docs site once Leah posts the copy.

Kevin: 👍 prioritize tests that assert UA-based fallback doesn't leak into new SDKs.

Jordan R: End state checklist before enforcement: docs published, email + blog post sent, console alias mapping visible, runtime flag in prod, telemetry dashboards active.

Samir: Noted. I'll update this thread with the staging deploy link and PR number when ready.

Leah P: Thanks.

Jordan R: :thumbsup:
